batch_scope: Phase 1 batch 1a: hash-pinned live-safe Component C engine wheel, packaging tree, and provenance record. Packaging only -- no adapter wiring, no application import, no live learner flow, no new scientific parameter. Governed by Component_C_Master_Build_Plan_v3.0.md Sections 3, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11 (Phase 1), 12, as amended by the owner's DEC-1/DEC-2/DEC-3 decisions and COR-1/COR-2 corrections recorded below. Batch 1b (the adapter at app/infrastructure/live_engine_c/adapter.py and the full-dotted-path architecture guard extension) is a separate, later work order; nothing under backend/app/ is touched by this batch.

package.vendor_prefix_note: This package uses the prabathi- prefix (attributes Component C's engine to its owner, Prabathi / Alwis L.P.M., IT22117878) while upadya-component-b-live-engine keeps the upadya- prefix (Component_C_Master_Build_Plan_v3.0 Section 12.1 item 5). The two coupled wheels carrying different vendor prefixes is DELIBERATE, not drift.
package.build_command: python -m build --wheel --no-isolation --outdir <dist> (setuptools==80.10.2, wheel==0.46.3, build==1.2.2.post1; built inside the exact application base image docker.io/library/python:3.11.15-slim-bookworm@sha256:b18992999dbe963a45a8a4da40ac2b1975be1a776d939d098c647482bcad5cba, not a merely-compatible local interpreter -- interpreter parity and line-ending parity, per Component_C_Master_Build_Plan_v3.0 Section 11 Phase 1 hard constraints and the C-21 precedent recorded in Component B's own manifest). Batch 1a specifically: the packaging tree was bind-mounted read-only at /src, copied to a writable container-internal path /build_src, and built there with --outdir pointed at a bind-mounted /dist -- so python -m build's own build/ and *.egg-info/ artefacts never touch the host filesystem or the committed source tree; only the finished .whl crosses the bind mount into backend/provenance/wheels/.
package.application_container_installation: NOT YET WIRED. Batch 1a adds this wheel to requirements.in/requirements.lock/Dockerfile/.dockerignore (see pin_locations below) so a rebuilt image installs it, but no application code imports it. That import boundary is Batch 1b's scope (app/infrastructure/live_engine_c/adapter.py), a separate, later work order.
package.application_code_import: NONE in this batch. Reserved for Batch 1b: app/infrastructure/live_engine_c/adapter.py, enforced by a full-dotted-path AST guard extension to backend/tests/test_be2_architecture_guards.py and a per-module ModuleNotFoundError test suite mirroring backend/tests/test_be3_live_engine_boundary.py.

trimmed_files.reason: REWORK (Phase 1 batch 1a, second pass): removed exactly three things relative to the pinned commit -- (1) the line `from .session import RunCSessionResult, run_c_session`; (2) the whole advance_session() function, the per-session driver that called run_c_session and returned RunCSessionResult; (3) _DRIVER_OWNED_SESSION_KWARGS, a module-level constant verified referenced ONLY inside advance_session's body and therefore dead once that function is gone. pipeline/session.py is never-ship (Component_C_Master_Build_Plan_v3.0 Section 6.1: it is the C6.0 run_c_session driver, excluded by Section 6.2's per-module packaging boundary). This file retains CLearnerSessionState, initial_learner_session_state, is_eligible_combined_handoff, and decide_next_session_phase -- the owner's CORRECTED trim authorization: Section 6.2's original two-symbol list (CLearnerSessionState, is_eligible_combined_handoff only) was incomplete and omitted initial_learner_session_state and decide_next_session_phase, both live-required (Cold-Start Bootstrap Readiness Assessment Section 5) and neither touching any never-ship module -- decide_next_session_phase in particular is the reviewed implementation of the C-16 Phase 4 phase-gate step and depends only on already-shipped selection/phase.py and selection/config.py. Two items are retained deliberately, not by oversight, despite losing their only in-file caller: SessionStateInputError (previously raised only inside advance_session, referenced nowhere else in the entire pinned tree including never-ship modules; kept because the owner's trim authorization names three items to remove, not four -- a public-API exception class is not removed unnamed) and the `from typing import Annotated, Any, Dict, Mapping, Tuple` import (Any/Mapping/Tuple become unused but the line itself depends on no never-ship module, so minimal-diff discipline leaves it untouched). _SEVEN_SKILLS was verified, not assumed, to remain live: it is referenced by CLearnerSessionState._spacing_uses_known_skills, a field validator on a kept class. After this removal, run_c_session, RunCSessionResult, advance_session, and _DRIVER_OWNED_SESSION_KWARGS are simply not bound names in this module's namespace (hasattr(module, name) is False for each), the same namespace-level guarantee backend/tests/test_be3_live_engine_boundary.py already relies on for Component B's trimmed files -- this is a deliberate namespace-level trim, not merely a source-text-substring absence claim; the string 'run_c_session' still appears in this file's PACKAGING NOTE prose describing what was removed.

dec_1_c22_validators_and_emit.decision: OMIT component_c_generator/c_to_3/emit.py from this package. Do NOT vendor validators/ as a second top-level package.
dec_1_c22_validators_and_emit.rationale: At the pin, c_to_3/emit.py is the only file on the original shipped list that imports a top-level package neither this wheel nor upadya-component-b-live-engine provides: `from validators.contract_validators import validate_payload, validate_payload_against_mapping`. validators/ is genuinely shared, not C-specific -- its PayloadKind is Literal['mapping','b_to_c','b_to_3','c_to_3'], so it validates B's payloads too. Vendoring it in C's wheel would make C its owner while C already depends on B for models/, creating a circular ownership the moment B ships adapters/* of its own. Verified safe to omit: emit.py is the only shipped file importing validators; the only importers of c_to_3.emit within component_c_generator are pipeline/session.py (never-ship) and, via c_to_3.inputs (not emit directly), pipeline/pilot.py (also never-ship); c_to_3/__init__.py is 35 bytes of `from __future__ import annotations` and needed no trim.
dec_1_c22_validators_and_emit.consequence: This wheel does not provide NoRealCSessionError or emit_c_to_3. Component_C_Master_Build_Plan_v3.0 Section 11 Phase 9 names emit_c_to_3 / NoRealCSessionError in its acceptance criteria (the SF-040 gate: 'emit_c_to_3 raises NoRealCSessionError when no real C session exists -- asserted'), so a Phase 9 rebuild and re-pin of this wheel is SCHEDULED, not merely possible -- most likely by extracting one shared wheel owning models/ + validators/ + schemas/, which would also resolve the pre-existing models/ asymmetry (B's wheel is the sole models/ owner today).
dec_1_c22_validators_and_emit.relationship_to_b_manifest: backend/provenance/component-b-live-engine-manifest.json's excluded_by_omission.modules separately lists 'validators (and validators/*)' as excluded from Component B's wheel. That exclusion was scoped to B's own reviewed capability closure at BE3/BF-4 and predates this decision. Component C's omission of c_to_3/emit.py (and, with it, the only C-side need for validators/) is an INDEPENDENT decision reached for the ownership reason above -- a later reader should not read either omission as drift from the other.

cor_2_five_pin_locations.why_not_eight: Component_C_Master_Build_Plan_v3.0 originally stated eight pin locations by analogy to Component B's count, which includes three tests/fixtures/runtime_bundle/*.json files. Those three fixtures exist because Component B's own runtime-bundle chain (BE3b) reads and checksum-verifies B's wheel at a schema location that declares 'generator' as a SINGLE object ($ref: #/$defs/sourceArtifact in backend/provenance/runtime-bundle.schema.json), not an array -- verified this batch. All three fixtures currently carry exactly one generator entry, pointing at upadya-component-b-live-engine. Component C's own runtime-bundle chain does not exist until Component C's Phase 2 ('Catalogue loader and runtime bundle'), which is explicitly out of scope for Phase 1. This batch does not add a C entry to any of the three fixtures. Phase 2 will carry the three fixture locations forward when C's runtime-bundle record is built.
